clue.text: Transport one or two

annotationWithheld.why: Transport one or two (5): 'one or two' gives BRACE (a pair) but no sense of 'Transport' plainly defines BRACE; the scan confirms the word, so the second definition cannot be shown

clue.text: Having perhaps won a bit as a sailing man

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A seaman who may have won a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' only links; 'perhaps' rearranges WON A BIT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: This ship's officer, often written bosun, is a seaman in charge of rigging.

clue.text: A large number work more than adequately

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Doing lots of jobs is more than enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Amply means abundantly, plenty.

clue.text: English farm animals in satirical verses

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
rams are male sheep on a farm

explanation.surface: English livestock appear in some witty poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Short witty poems with a satirical sting.

clue.text: Setting out about fifty would be most surprising

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the word for setting out is wrapped round the numeral

parts.note: setting out on a journey is starting
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone says it would be astonishing if a party of fifty set out together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be' only links wordplay to definition; 'about' puts L inside STARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is highly astonishing, enough to make one jump.

clue.text: Pause for a bracer.

explanation.surface: Stopping for a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A bracer is a support, as stays are supports in a corset or ship's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to remain; a stay is a prop or support.

clue.text: "An undevout —— is mad" (Young)

parts.note: the missing word completes a line from Edward Young's Night Thoughts about one who studies the stars

explanation.surface: A quotation with a gap for the solver to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Young, an 18th-century English poet, wrote this line in Night Thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: The line says a stargazer who lacks faith must be insane.

clue.text: In time a painter will get much abuse

indicators.note: In shows the painter's letters going into the word for time

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide
RA means a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist will be harshly criticised eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' wants to be T, but here it is the old word seen in Yuletide and Eastertide; 'In' places the Royal Academician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of criticism.

clue.text: Clever in acquiring information on unpaid debts

parts.note: gen is slang for information
IOUs are notes of debt

explanation.surface: Someone shrewd collects the facts about bad debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious means inventive and resourceful.

clue.text: Song about the black earth

indicators.note: about puts the song's letters around the letter for black

parts.note: a glee is a part-song
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A ballad about dark soil.
explanation.walkthrough: GLEBE is land belonging to a parish church; poetically, soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is a poetic word for land or soil.

clue.text: Job-seeker put in charge in a phosphorus factory

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

indicators.note: put here means placed inside, so the abbreviation is set within the word for a works

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: A candidate for a job is made a supervisor at a chemical works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in charge' reads as a promotion, but 'in charge' is a standard abbreviation and 'put' places it inside the factory; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies for a post is a candidate seeking work.

clue.text: Villain making lament about turn-over

indicators.note: about signals that the word for lament goes around the other piece

parts.note: to rue is to lament or regret

indicators.note: over, joined to turn by a hyphen, says the word for turn is flipped over

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A villain bemoans a sudden change of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-over' looks like one word, a pastry or a change; split it so 'over' flips the word for turn, which 'about' then places inside the word for lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a scoundrel or rascal, a dishonest person.

clue.text: People speaking of a mystery writer

explanation.surface: Readers chat about an author of detective fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L. Sayers was an English writer of detective novels featuring Lord Peter Wimsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who say things are talkers; Dorothy L. Sayers wrote detective stories.

clue.text: Not favouring stupid contract

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
dense means slow-witted

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a foolish agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun, an agreement, but it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to make smaller or more compact, i.e. shrink.

clue.text: Manual worker and a graduate involved in weighty issue

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the degree goes into the other pieces

parts.note: a stone is a unit of weight, 14 pounds
a son is one's issue, a child
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A labourer and a university graduate caught up in a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight equal to 14 pounds; 'involved in' puts the degree between the weight and the child.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cuts and builds with stone works with his hands.

clue.text: Taking over with a certain arrogance

explanation.surface: A takeover carried out with a confident swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: The taking on of power or office is so called; presumption, a cocky overconfidence, is its other sense.

clue.text: A foreigner without money —- it makes him choke!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the stranger's letters surround the money

parts.note: a stranger is a foreigner or outsider
L stands for pound, money

explanation.surface: A broke outsider is so desperate he chokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside; L (pound sterling) goes inside STRANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who throttles victims causes them to gasp for breath.

clue.text: An expedition to Abraham's birthplace

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees is the city Abraham came from in Genesis

explanation.surface: A journey to the ancient city where the patriarch was born.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey or trip visiting several places is an expedition of a sort.

clue.text: Put on fresh clothing and made up

explanation.surface: Someone changed outfits and applied makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed again; redressed also means remedied or compensated for a wrong.

clue.text: Very quiet in drink — quiet, that is, when food's available

indicators.note: in signals the very-quiet letters going inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
PP, pianissimo, means very quietly in music
P, piano, means quietly
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Drinkers keep hushed, at least while there's something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: PP and P are musical directions; 'when' and 's available' link the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit dessert in pastry is a dish to eat.

clue.text: "Service not included" is the usual thing

parts.note: no is a negative, not
RM, the Royal Marines, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill's line that tips are extra is standard practice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a menu; 'Service' is a fighting service, and 'included' only links NO to RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard, what is typical or expected.

clue.text: Put in extra big E in printed form

indicators.note: printed form suggests reshaping, so these letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, an extra-large clothing size

explanation.surface: An instruction to a typesetter to insert a large capital letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges OS, E and PRINTED together; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to insert something between other things.

clue.text: It may appear a hero's landed!

indicators.note: says what appears may be a rearrangement of the words given

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped and the s kept

explanation.surface: A champion comes home in triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may appear' rearranges HERO'S into SHORE, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land, having landed.

clue.text: Pass a portion that's quite liberal

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: Handing over a share is rather generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift or sum is a generous one.

clue.text: Sound American soil-improver

parts.note: a hum is a sound
US means American

explanation.surface: A healthy American fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like healthy; it is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Decomposed organic matter enriches soil.

clue.text: A plug being wrongly fitted, note serious complaint

indicators.note: a plug wired wrongly has its parts in the wrong places, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An electrical plug installed badly gives rise to a grave grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' is an illness here, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic disease is a dreadful illness, and complaint means ailment.

clue.text: Woman writing Greek letter from Greece

indicators.note: from shows the country abbreviation coming first

parts.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greece
eta is the seventh Greek letter

explanation.surface: A lady writing a letter home from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' and 'from' read as a letter home, but 'writing' is only a link and 'from' puts the country's abbreviation first.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the actress Garbo.

clue.text: Control knob

explanation.surface: A switch on a panel.
explanation.definitionFit: To boss is to direct; a boss is also a round raised stud.

clue.text: One may see some dismal modern buildings in Sweden

definitions.text: One may see some dismal modern buildings in Sweden

indicators.note: some of means only part of the run dismal modern is used

explanation.surface: A traveller might spot gloomy new architecture in a Scandinavian town.
explanation.definitionFit: This port city in southern Sweden, facing Copenhagen, has modern buildings.

clue.text: A way to put down really up-to-date information

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
to oppress is to put down or subjugate

explanation.surface: A method of recording the very latest news.
explanation.walkthrough: STOP PRESS is late news added to a newspaper after printing started.
explanation.definitionFit: Late news inserted into a paper at the last moment is the freshest available.

clue.text: Men of rank, can deal with greatness

indicators.note: dealing out cards shuffles them, so the letters are redistributed

explanation.surface: Ranked officers can cope with fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men of rank' suggests nobility, but the rank is military: NCOs.
explanation.definitionFit: These NCOs hold a rank above corporal in the army.

clue.text: Beast died after impetuous rush

indicators.note: after puts the abbreviation for died at the end

parts.note: elan is dash or vigour

explanation.surface: An animal died after a headlong charge.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African antelope is an animal.
